Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Apply explicit corrections to the final stated intent. Preserve meaningful filler-like words and unfinished thoughts. Apply clearly spoken punctuation and list cues. Keep the supplied language.", "input": "for saturday's neighborhood weather station update, please tell people the open table starts at nine by the east gate. the rain gauge readings are already in the blue notebook, and we still need somebody to check the wind vane before the school group arrives. i had planned for Celia to do that, no, sorry, Omar is checking the wind vane; Celia is taking the thermometer readings. the spare batteries are in the metal box under the folding table, and the sign-in sheet is clipped to the board beside it. first, ask visitors to write down the time they arrive, then show them how to read the outdoor thermometer without touching the bulb. we should mention that the cloud cover estimate is only a quick observation, not a forecast. if the path is wet, please move the demonstration to the paved area near the library entrance. i think the small table can hold the notebooks and pencils, but the rain gauge chart needs to stay dry, so put it inside the clear sleeve. oh, and the school group asked whether they can bring their own ruler to compare the rain totals. i haven't checked if we have enough clipboards for everyone, so leave a few blank spaces on the sign-in sheet for walk-ins too.", "output": "For Saturday's neighborhood weather station update, please tell people the open table starts at nine by the east gate. The rain gauge readings are already in the blue notebook, and we still need somebody to check the wind vane before the school group arrives. Omar is checking the wind vane; Celia is taking the thermometer readings. The spare batteries are in the metal box under the folding table, and the sign-in sheet is clipped to the board beside it. First, ask visitors to write down the time they arrive, then show them how to read the outdoor thermometer without touching the bulb. We should mention that the cloud cover estimate is only a quick observation, not a forecast. If the path is wet, please move the demonstration to the paved area near the library entrance. I think the small table can hold the notebooks and pencils, but the rain gauge chart needs to stay dry, so put it inside the clear sleeve. Oh, and the school group asked whether they can bring their own ruler to compare the rain totals. I haven't checked if we have enough clipboards for everyone, so leave a few blank spaces on the sign-in sheet for walk-ins too."}]
